sections.content:
Independent research guided by an Economic Faculty. Candidates should have regular meetings and keep a close connection with their supervisor throughout the semester. By the end of the term, candidates need to submit a minimum 7 pages of research proposal, and present it at the thesis workshop while addressing inquiries from other faculty members.

ECON4800: Honors Thesis II w/ Byoungchan has been updated

WARNING: If you are considering to do SBMT4000 under an economic professor, please spend a minute reading friend's review: https://ust.space/review/SBMT4000
sections.teaching:
The program coordinator is Prof. AU, Pak Hung, who will receive your final proposal and schedule the presentation workshop.

I chose Prof. Lee as my supervisor although I have never taken his courses (ECON 2/3123) before. He has certainly enjoyed a great reputation for creating a supportive and caring atmosphere at every course he is responsible for. People would praise his generosity for:
1. No attendance requirements, but provides recordings along with the lecture schedule
2. Releasing a bunch of past papers sufficient for exams
3. Distributes the max Å-ranges as he could
4. Caring, friendly, and supportive (In any sense)

After four months working with him, I would admit choosing him is one of the BEST decisions I have ever made in UST,

Don't panic if you have not determined the topic. Tell him, and he could lock the right paper within minutes.  
What if my theoretical foundations are insufficient? No worries, just self-study on your own, and address your confusions in weekly meetings.  He would write down the detailed math derivations on paper until you grasped the key. I was self reading VAR slides by Prof. WANG Peng and stumbled to proceed due to my poor linear algebra foundation. He told me not to worry and keep my comfortable pace because he also got stuck on some math as a student T_T.

He is happy to help with anything that could be bothering. Like how to prepare math for academia, or whether to go on an exchange in the fourth year... He will share his own experiences along the way.

Furthermore, he expects us to make mistakes. Although my preliminary results are full of loopholes, he would still encourage me to present so I could learn the insights from other professors.

Several days before the presentation, he showed me some standards for an excellent academic presentation. Something I remembered clearly is never to omit anything shown on the sides, including details in figures and the table of contents. (Thank heavens I can put extra things on my LABU learning portfolio hahahahahah)

"So, follow your gut feeling and try to enjoy the presentation.
Look forward to listening to your presentation tomorrow!"

Thanks, Prof. Lee! One of the best tutors in my life!
sections.grading:
Graded P or F. As long as you submit an approved proposal by your supervisor and present your slides without pissing off other faculties, you will be guaranteed a pass.

So, DON'T GIVE UP!
sections.workload:
HEAVY AF. Way beyond 2 credits for those conducting their independent research for the first time.

Warning: It would be way better to have regular meetings (like once or twice every two weeks) to spread your workload evenly across the whole semester. If you pile things up in the final weeks, you will undoubtedly be doomed.

However, the difficulty is only the average for an independent (individual) research project. Gven that it's the first time for most undergrad students to gain exposure to serious academic papers and self-study some theories to bridge the gap, things could be more challenging than a 3-4 credit econ elective course.
